trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out to (7,4,4), to (7,6,2) or to (6,4,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,4,4).
I can't rule out to (7,4,6) or to (7,6,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,4,6).
I can't rule out to (7,2,6) or to (6,4,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,2,6).
I can't rule out to (6,1,6) or to (6,2,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,1,6).
Going to (4,1,6) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (6,2,7) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,1,4).
Going to (6,1,2) would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (7,2,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,2).
Going to number 5 leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (6,1,2).
I can't rule out to (6,2,1) or to (4,1,2) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,2,1).
Going to (4,2,1) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,4,1).
The line must go to (6,6,1): to (4,4,1) is number 11, which comes later.
I can't rule out to (7,6,2), to (6,7,2) or to (4,6,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,6,2).
Going to (6,7,2) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes to (7,6,4).
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out to (6,6,7) or to (6,7,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,6,7).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (6,7,6) would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (4,6,7) would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (6,4,7) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (to (6,6,7) from number 6) was wrong, so the line must go to (6,7,6).
The line must go to (6,6,7): to (4,7,6) is number 19, which comes later; to (6,7,4) is number 16, which comes later.
Going to (4,6,7) would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,4,7).
The line must go to (6,2,7): to (4,4,7) is number 20, which comes later.
Going to (4,1,6), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2,7). So the line goes to (2,2,7).
Going to (2,1,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,2,6).
Going to (1,4,6) would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (2,1,6).
Cell (4,1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1,4).
Going to (4,1,2) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,1,4).
Number 10 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (4,1,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,2,1).
Going to (4,6,1) would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (2,4,1).
Number 12 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going to (1,4,6) would strand number 14: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (1,6,4) would strand number 14: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (1,4,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,6,2).

Going to (1,6,4), the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,7,2); going to number 15, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6,1). So the line goes to (2,7,2).

Going to (2,7,4) would strand number 15: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (4,7,2) would leave both cell (6,7,2) and cell (4,6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (2,6,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,6,1).
Cell (6,7,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,7,4).
Cell (1,6,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,6,6).
Cell (1,4,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,4,7).
Cell (2,7,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,7,6).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
